description: A comprehensive study guide covering the most frequently asked computer abbreviations, their full forms, and their core functions, optimized for competitive exam preparation.

sections.title: Hardware and System Abbreviations
sections.description: Crucial acronyms related to the physical components and foundational boot processes of a computer system.

key_associations.extra_info: Firmware embedded on the motherboard that initializes hardware during the booting process.
A battery-powered chip that stores basic system settings, including the system time and date.
An electronic circuit that efficiently converts and supplies the appropriate power to various PC components.
Provides emergency battery backup to prevent sudden shutdowns and data loss during power failures.
A standard type of connection for video devices such as monitors and projectors.

sections.title: Networking and Internet Abbreviations
sections.description: Essential terms related to web communication, data transmission, and network security.

key_associations.extra_info: The foundational protocol for transmitting and receiving data across the World Wide Web.
The unique address used to locate a specific webpage or resource on the internet.
The core suite of communication protocols used to interconnect network devices on the internet.
A company that provides individuals and organizations access to the internet (e.g., Jio, Airtel).
Creates a secure, encrypted connection over a public network to protect user identity and data.

sections.title: Data Representation and Storage
sections.description: Acronyms associated with digital storage hardware and text encoding standards.

key_associations.associated_with: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
key_associations.extra_info: A universal character encoding standard used to represent text in computers and other devices.

key_associations.associated_with: Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code
key_associations.extra_info: An 8-bit character encoding system primarily used in IBM mainframe and midrange computer systems.
A modern, high-speed storage device that uses flash memory, lacking the moving parts of a traditional HDD.
A standard unit of measurement for data transfer speed over a network or internet connection.

sections.title: Software and File Formats
sections.description: Abbreviations for operating systems, user interfaces, and widely used digital files.

key_associations.extra_info: A visual way of interacting with a computer using items such as windows, icons, and menus, instead of text commands.
The primary system software that manages computer hardware, software resources, and provides common services (e.g., Windows, Linux).
A universal file format developed by Adobe to present and share documents reliably, independent of software or hardware.
The most widely used image compression standard for storing and transmitting digital photographs.
A set of rules and protocols that allows different software applications to communicate and interact with each other.
